name: “Beautiful Gate” of the Jerusalem Temple
summary: Gate named in Acts 3 at which a man is healed. Which physical Temple gate the term designates is debated.

confidence.explanation: Acts names the gate, but no surviving inscription or uncontested archaeological identification fixes it to a specific gate of the Herodian complex.

locationNote: No normal pin. Candidate identifications such as the Nicanor/Corinthian gate traditions are not treated as established.

name: Solomon’s Portico / Colonnade
summary: Temple-complex portico named in Acts as a gathering location.

confidence.explanation: The eastern colonnade of the Herodian Temple complex provides the broad setting, but the precise built footprint is not independently recoverable today.

locationNote: Broad Temple Mount context only; no exact surviving point is claimed.

name: Akeldama / Field of Blood
summary: Jerusalem-area place associated in Acts 1 with the field connected to Judas.

confidence.explanation: Later tradition places Akeldama in the Hinnom Valley south of Jerusalem, but the precise first-century parcel is not recoverable.

locationNote: Unpinned textual/traditional location in the southern Jerusalem landscape.

name: Location of Stephen’s stoning
summary: Acts places Stephen’s execution outside the city but does not identify a recoverable gate or exact spot.

confidence.explanation: Later “St Stephen’s Gate” traditions are not sufficient to establish the first-century execution location.

locationNote: No normal pin; outside-Jerusalem narrative geography only.

name: Lydda / Lod
summary: Judean plain city where Acts narrates Peter’s healing of Aeneas.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Lydda is securely identified with Lod; the house or precise location of the Acts episode is unknown.

name: Azotus / Ashdod
summary: Coastal city named as Philip’s location after the encounter on the Gaza road.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Ashdod/Azotus is securely located in the Ashdod area; Acts does not identify a building or route through the city.

name: Sharon Plain
summary: Coastal plain named in Acts 9 in connection with Lydda and the spread of the movement.

confidence.explanation: The physical coastal plain is established; the point is a display anchor for a broad landscape, not a center.

locationNote: Display anchor only for the broad Sharon coastal plain.

name: Antipatris
summary: Herodian/Roman city on the Jerusalem–Caesarea corridor where Paul’s military escort stops according to Acts 23.

confidence.explanation: Antipatris is widely identified with the Tell Aphek/Ras al-‘Ayn area; the city’s general location is strong though the exact overnight stopping point is unknown.

name: Straight Street — Damascus
summary: Acts names the “street called Straight” in Damascus. A long east–west Roman street axis underlies the traditional identification.

confidence.explanation: The Roman decumanus alignment is archaeologically/topographically plausible, but Acts’ exact house on the street is not known.

locationNote: Approximate Roman street-axis anchor, not an identified first-century doorway.

name: House of Judas in Damascus
summary: House on Straight Street where Acts places Saul after the Damascus encounter.

confidence.explanation: Acts names the householder Judas, but the specific building is not recoverable archaeologically.

locationNote: No normal pin. Later devotional identifications are not treated as established.

name: Tarsus
summary: Major Cilician city identified by Acts as Paul’s birthplace and later location.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Tarsus is securely identified with modern Tarsus; much of the Roman city lies beneath later occupation.

name: Syria and Cilicia corridor
summary: Broad regional corridor named in Acts 15 as Paul and Silas strengthen communities.

confidence.explanation: Syria and Cilicia are historical regions/provinces; the point is only a broad display anchor and does not imply a single road.

locationNote: Display anchor for a broad regional corridor.

name: “Arabia” in Galatians 1
summary: Region Paul says he went to after his calling, before returning to Damascus. The territorial meaning is broad and the route is not described.

confidence.explanation: In Paul’s first-century context “Arabia” may relate to Nabataean territory, but Galatians does not identify a city or itinerary.

locationNote: No exact pin; a broad Nabataean/Arabian context is shown only as interpretation.

interpretations.title: Nabataean Arabia
interpretations.summary: A common historical interpretation places Paul somewhere within the Nabataean sphere south/east of Damascus; the specific destination is unknown.

name: Cyprus
summary: Island crossed by Barnabas and Paul on the first missionary journey.

confidence.explanation: Cyprus is certain; the display point represents the island rather than a precise center of activity.

locationNote: Island-level display anchor.

name: Salamis, Cyprus
summary: Major eastern Cypriot city where Acts says Barnabas and Paul proclaimed in Jewish synagogues.

confidence.explanation: The archaeological city of Salamis is securely located north of modern Famagusta.

name: Paphos
summary: Western Cypriot administrative center where Acts places the encounter with Sergius Paulus and Bar-Jesus/Elymas.

confidence.explanation: Roman Nea Paphos is securely located; the precise praetorium or meeting place of Acts 13 is not identified.

name: Perga
summary: Pamphylian city visited on the first missionary journey and again on the return.

confidence.explanation: The extensive ruins of Perga securely identify the Roman city.

name: Attalia
summary: Pamphylian port from which Paul and Barnabas sail back to Antioch according to Acts 14.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Attalia is securely identified with Antalya’s old-city/harbor area.

name: Antioch near Pisidia
summary: Roman-colony city in southern Galatia/Pisidia where Acts 13–14 narrates an extended synagogue and civic episode.

confidence.explanation: The site at Yalvaç is securely identified as Antioch; the exact synagogue of Acts is not identified.

name: Iconium
summary: Central Anatolian city visited by Paul and Barnabas in Acts 14 and again in later journeys.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Iconium is securely identified with Konya, though much of the ancient city lies under the modern settlement.

name: Lystra
summary: Lycaonian city associated with Paul’s first journey, the stoning episode, and Timothy’s home region.

confidence.explanation: Lystra is widely located at/near the Zoldera mound by Hatunsaray, but the archaeological identification is less monumental than cities such as Ephesus or Corinth.

locationNote: Strong scholarly location tradition; shown as a candidate-site rather than an absolute survey certainty.

name: Derbe
summary: Lycaonian city reached on the first missionary journey and revisited in Acts 16. The exact archaeological identification remains debated.

confidence.explanation: Ancient sources establish Derbe in Lycaonia, but modern site identification has shifted among proposals; the textual place therefore remains unpinned.

locationNote: No normal pin. Kerti Höyük is shown separately as a major modern candidate.

name: Kerti Höyük — Derbe candidate
summary: Major modern candidate for ancient Derbe.

confidence.explanation: Kerti Höyük is often favored in modern discussion, but the project does not equate the candidate with the textual city as an established fact.

locationNote: Candidate used for route visualization only.

name: Galatia — Pauline / Acts regional context
summary: Broad central-Anatolian context relevant to Acts and the addressees of Galatians. The identity of Paul’s “Galatians” in relation to provincial versus ethnic geography is debated.

confidence.explanation: Roman Galatia had changing administrative extent, and the North/South Galatia question affects reconstruction of the letter’s audience.

locationNote: Broad display anchor only; not a border claim.

name: Alexandria Troas
summary: Major Troad port city where Acts places Paul before crossing to Macedonia and again on the return journey.

confidence.explanation: The substantial archaeological city is securely identified on the Aegean coast.

name: Samothrace
summary: Aegean island named as an overnight point on the voyage from Troas to Neapolis.

confidence.explanation: The island is certain; Acts does not specify an anchorage.

locationNote: Island-level anchor; exact anchorage unknown.

name: Neapolis (Macedonia)
summary: Macedonian port of Philippi, generally identified with modern Kavala.

confidence.explanation: The ancient port is securely associated with Kavala’s location, though shoreline and harbor details changed over time.

name: Philippi
summary: Roman colony in Macedonia where Acts narrates Lydia, imprisonment, and a new community.

confidence.explanation: The archaeological site of Philippi is securely identified and extensively excavated.

name: Riverside prayer-place near Philippi
summary: Acts places the encounter with Lydia outside the city gate by a river or watercourse where prayer was customary.

confidence.explanation: The Gangites/Angites river landscape is plausible, but no archaeological marker identifies the exact prayer place.

locationNote: No exact pin. Modern commemorative sites are not treated as archaeological proof.

name: Prison in Philippi — Acts narrative
summary: Acts narrates Paul and Silas imprisoned in Philippi, but no excavated building can be securely identified as that prison.

confidence.explanation: Later local identifications are devotional traditions, not conclusive archaeology.

locationNote: Unpinned within the established city of Philippi.

name: Amphipolis
summary: Macedonian city passed through on the route from Philippi toward Thessalonica.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Amphipolis is securely located on the Strymon River.

name: Apollonia in Macedonia
summary: City on the Via Egnatia named between Amphipolis and Thessalonica in Acts 17.

confidence.explanation: The general Lake Volvi / modern Apollonia area is accepted, but the exact ancient urban footprint is less securely defined than Amphipolis or Thessalonica.

locationNote: Approximate city-area anchor.

name: Thessalonica
summary: Major Macedonian port and provincial center where Acts narrates synagogue preaching and opposition; recipient city of 1–2 Thessalonians.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Thessalonica lies beneath modern Thessaloniki and is securely identified.

name: Berea / Beroea
summary: Macedonian city where Acts praises receptive synagogue hearers before Paul travels toward Athens.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Beroea is securely identified with modern Veria.

name: Athens
summary: Major Greek city where Acts narrates Paul engaging synagogue, marketplace, philosophers, and the Areopagus.

confidence.explanation: Athens is secure; individual meeting spots in Acts are not all archaeologically identifiable.

name: Areopagus — hill/council context
summary: Acts 17 says Paul was brought “to the Areopagus.” The term can refer to the council/body and, by extension, its setting; the exact speech spot is not certain.

confidence.explanation: The Hill of Ares is a securely located topographic feature, but the narrative wording does not compel the conclusion that Paul stood at one exact point on the hill.

locationNote: Physical Areopagus hill shown; event location within/with the Areopagus council remains interpretive.

name: Corinth
summary: Roman colony and Achaian center where Paul spends an extended period according to Acts and which receives major Pauline correspondence.

confidence.explanation: Roman Corinth is securely identified at the excavated city below Acrocorinth.

name: Bema in the Roman forum at Corinth
summary: Monumental speaking/judgment platform in Corinth’s forum, often discussed in relation to Gallio’s hearing of Paul.

confidence.explanation: The bema structure is archaeologically established, but Acts does not identify a specific surviving platform; using it as Paul’s exact hearing location remains interpretive.

locationNote: Established forum monument; event correlation is possible, not proven.

name: Cenchreae
summary: Eastern port of Corinth named in Acts and Romans.

confidence.explanation: The port site at modern Kechries is securely identified, with submerged and excavated remains.

name: Achaia — Roman provincial context
summary: Roman province including Corinth and Athens in the first century CE.

confidence.explanation: The province is historical, but the display point/polygon is generalized and not a surveyed border for every year.

locationNote: Broad provincial orientation only.

name: Ephesus
summary: Major city of Roman Asia where Acts places Paul for an extended ministry and a major civic disturbance.

confidence.explanation: Ephesus is one of the best-preserved Greco-Roman cities in the region; the theater and Artemision are independently established.

name: Great Theater of Ephesus
summary: Large theater associated with the civic assembly scene in Acts 19.

confidence.explanation: The theater is archaeologically established and fits the type of civic venue described; Acts does not preserve a seat-by-seat location.

name: Hall of Tyrannus
summary: Lecture hall named in Acts 19 as a place where Paul reasoned daily in Ephesus.

confidence.explanation: No excavated building can be securely identified as the hall of Tyrannus.

locationNote: Unpinned within Ephesus.

name: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
summary: Major sanctuary central to Ephesus’s identity and to the economic/religious context of Acts 19.

confidence.explanation: The Artemision site is securely located and archaeologically investigated; Acts does not say Paul entered the sanctuary.

name: Asia — Roman provincial context
summary: Roman province of Asia, repeatedly named in Acts and Pauline correspondence.

confidence.explanation: The province is historical; the point is a display anchor and context polygons are generalized across a changing administrative landscape.

locationNote: Broad provincial orientation only.

name: Miletus
summary: Ionian port city where Acts 20 places Paul’s meeting with elders from Ephesus.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Miletus is securely identified and extensively excavated; coastline has shifted significantly through silting.

name: Assos
summary: Troad city where Acts says Paul joined his companions by ship after traveling overland.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Assos is securely located at Behramkale.

name: Mitylene
summary: City on Lesbos named in Acts 20 as an overnight maritime stop.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Mitylene is securely identified with modern Mytilene.

name: Chios
summary: Aegean island named in Acts 20 as a sailing waypoint.

confidence.explanation: The island is certain; Acts does not state an exact harbor landing.

locationNote: Island-level route anchor only.

name: Samos
summary: Aegean island named in Acts 20 as a sailing waypoint.

confidence.explanation: The island is certain; exact anchorage is not specified.

locationNote: Island-level route anchor only.

name: Cos
summary: Island stop named in Acts 21 during Paul’s voyage toward Jerusalem.

confidence.explanation: The island and ancient city are securely located; the route line is schematic.

name: Patara
summary: Lycian port where Paul’s party changes ships for the voyage toward Phoenicia.

confidence.explanation: Patara is securely identified and archaeologically well documented as a major Lycian port.

name: Myra
summary: Lycian city/port region where the centurion transfers Paul to an Alexandrian grain ship bound west.

confidence.explanation: Myra and its harbor at Andriake are securely identified; Acts names Myra but not the precise berth.

name: Cnidus
summary: Promontory/city region named in Acts 27 as the ship struggles westward before turning toward Crete.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Cnidus is securely located on the Datça peninsula; the ship’s exact offshore track cannot be recovered.

name: Crete
summary: Large island along whose southern coast the Alexandrian ship sails in Acts 27.

confidence.explanation: The island is certain; route geometry is illustrative.

locationNote: Island-level display anchor.

name: Fair Havens, Crete
summary: Harbor named in Acts 27 near Lasea, generally identified with modern Kaloi Limenes.

confidence.explanation: The traditional/topographic identification with Kaloi Limenes is strong, but harbor morphology and exact ancient facilities require caution.

name: Lasea
summary: Cretan city said to be near Fair Havens in Acts 27.

confidence.explanation: Ruins near Fair Havens are commonly associated with Lasea, but the urban identification is less secure than major excavated cities.

name: Phoenix / Phoenice, Crete
summary: Harbor the crew hoped to reach for winter in Acts 27. The exact harbor identification is debated.

confidence.explanation: The text gives directional harbor characteristics, but modern proposals differ; no single point is treated as established.

locationNote: Unpinned textual harbor; Loutro and other south-Cretan proposals remain interpretive.

name: Cauda / Clauda — Gavdos
summary: Island passed under for shelter during the storm in Acts 27, commonly identified with Gavdos.

confidence.explanation: Gavdos is the standard historical-geographic identification of Cauda/Clauda; the ship’s exact lee-side track is unknown.

name: Malta / Melite
summary: Island identified in Acts 28 after the shipwreck. Malta is the mainstream identification of Melite.

confidence.explanation: Linguistic, geographic, and navigational considerations strongly support Malta, while the exact landfall within the island remains disputed.

locationNote: Island-level anchor; not an exact wreck site.

name: Exact shipwreck site on Malta
summary: Acts describes a bay with a beach but does not name a bay. Later traditions identify locations such as St Paul’s Bay.

confidence.explanation: No archaeological evidence securely identifies the precise Acts 27 wreck site; traditional bays remain hypotheses.

locationNote: No normal pin. The atlas deliberately does not equate St Paul’s Bay with a proven wreck site.

interpretations.title: St Paul’s Bay tradition
interpretations.summary: Longstanding Maltese tradition; navigational reconstructions can make the area plausible, but the biblical text and archaeology do not prove the exact bay.

name: Syracuse
summary: Sicilian city where Acts 28 says the voyage stopped for three days.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Syracuse is securely identified; the exact harbor berth is not known.

name: Rhegium
summary: Italian city at the Strait of Messina, a one-day stop on the voyage to Rome.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Rhegium is securely identified with Reggio Calabria.

name: Puteoli
summary: Major Bay of Naples port where Acts says Paul stayed seven days with believers before continuing overland to Rome.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Puteoli is securely identified with Pozzuoli and preserves substantial Roman remains.

name: Forum of Appius / Appii Forum
summary: Station on the Via Appia where Roman believers meet Paul according to Acts 28.

confidence.explanation: The ancient station is generally located in the Pontine plain along the Via Appia; the precise meeting point is not recoverable.

name: Three Taverns
summary: Via Appia station where Acts says another group of believers met Paul.

confidence.explanation: Ancient itineraries support a station south of Rome, but modern exact localization is debated.

locationNote: Unpinned road-station location; no exact modern marker is treated as certain.

name: Paul’s rented lodging in Rome
summary: Acts ends with Paul living under guard in rented quarters in Rome for two years.

confidence.explanation: Acts gives no address, and later church traditions do not securely identify the rented lodging.

locationNote: No normal pin; Rome is the secure city-level setting.

name: Colossae
summary: Lycus Valley city addressed by Colossians and associated with Philemon’s network; Acts does not narrate a visit by Paul.

confidence.explanation: The mound of ancient Colossae near Honaz is securely identified, though it has been less extensively excavated than Laodicea or Ephesus.

name: Laodicea on the Lycus
summary: Lycus Valley city mentioned in Colossians and later Revelation.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Laodicea is securely identified near modern Denizli and extensively excavated.

name: Hierapolis
summary: Lycus Valley city named in Colossians 4 alongside Laodicea and Colossae.

confidence.explanation: Ancient Hierapolis is securely identified at Pamukkale.

name: Illyricum in Romans 15
summary: Western Balkan region Paul names as the limit of his preaching “as far as Illyricum.” The phrase does not establish a specific city visit.

confidence.explanation: Illyricum is a historical regional/provincial term with changing borders; the atlas uses a broad anchor only.

locationNote: Broad display anchor; no exact Pauline itinerary is inferred.

name: Phrygia — Acts regional context
summary: Broad inland Anatolian region named in Acts as part of Paul’s travel context. Its administrative/geographic extent varied across periods.

confidence.explanation: Phrygia is a historical region, but this point is only a display anchor and does not define a surveyed first-century border.

locationNote: Broad regional anchor only; not a city or exact route point.

name: Macedonia — Acts regional context
summary: Roman provincial/regional context for repeated Pauline travel. Acts sometimes names Macedonia without listing every city visited.

confidence.explanation: Macedonia is historically secure; the point is a display anchor and the associated polygon is a generalized orientation layer.

locationNote: Broad regional anchor only; not an assertion that Paul stopped at this coordinate.
